quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: If your tires lose contact with the road, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down by shifting to a lower gear.
Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your tires lose contact with the road, ease off the gas pedal. Do not use the brakes or try to turn until your tires grip the road again.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: Passing is not permitted.
You can pass on the right when the road ahead is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline means you can cross it to pass another vehicle on the left if there is no oncoming traffic. Never cross a solid yellow centerline to pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. You must stop if traffic requires it.

questions.question: When driving to an unfamiliar place, you should:

options.text: Depend on road signs to find your way.
Plan your trip before you start driving.
Only know generally where your destination is.
Always choose the most direct route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Plan your trip in advance when driving to an unfamiliar area. Check your destination on a map before you start driving instead of starting with only a general idea.

questions.question: When two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different roads, which must yield?

options.text: Either one
The vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the right
Neither

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right. This applies at both controlled and uncontrolled intersections.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Always drive at the speed limit.
Use cruise control to keep steady speed.
Follow other cars more closely.
Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction on slippery surfaces. Reduce your speed and do not use cruise control on slippery roads.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a green arrow traffic light?

options.text: Merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
Turn in the direction of the arrow after letting other traffic and pedestrians pass.
Drive straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn in the direction of the arrow after letting other traffic and pedestrians pass.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane and yield to any vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection.

questions.question: When must you use your headlights?

options.text: When you cannot see 100 feet ahead.
When you cannot see 300 feet ahead.
When you cannot see 500 feet ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you cannot see 500 feet ahead.
questions.explanation: You must use headlights from sunset to sunrise. You must also use them any time you cannot see 500 feet or more ahead.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop and wait for the green light.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Stop and yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, yield the right-of-way, and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Roundabout ahead.
Lane ends, merge left.
Turn around.
Curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Roundabout ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a roundabout is ahead. Enter slowly and yield to traffic already in the roundabout.

questions.question: You are driving on an interstate. Traffic is merging from on-ramps on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Change lanes to the left.
Slow down.
Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to the left.
questions.explanation: Move to the left lane when you see an on-ramp ahead. This gives cars room to enter the highway safely.

questions.question: You are parallel parking between two cars. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Pull up next to the car in front of the parking space.
Back up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up next to the car in front of the parking space.
questions.explanation: Stop your car next to the car in front of the empty space. Check your mirrors and signal before turning your wheels to park.

questions.question: Roads and highways freeze before ramps and bridges.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Ramps and bridges freeze first because they are exposed to cold air from all sides. Drive slowly and carefully when crossing bridges in freezing weather.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop your car?

options.text: Signal lights.
Other cars on the road.
The time of day.
The condition of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The condition of the road.
questions.explanation: Road conditions greatly affect how quickly you can stop. Slow down on wet, icy, or damaged roads. Driving too fast on slippery roads makes it hard to stop safely.

questions.question: You see a steady yellow arrow at a traffic light. What should you do?

options.text: Merge in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
Turn left after checking for oncoming cars and pedestrians.
You have the right of way. Oncoming traffic must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop your car unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: How fast should you drive?

options.text: At the same speed as the cars around you.
At the speed limit.
At a speed that is safe for road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a speed that is safe for road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Always drive at a speed that is safe for the current road and weather. Never drive faster than the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: You are turning left from a two-way street. Where should you position your car?

options.text: Near the right side of the road.
Near the center line.
On the left side of the center line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the center line.
questions.explanation: Position your car close to the center line before turning left. Begin your turn just before the center of the intersection. Turn into the first available legal lane.

questions.question: What does a speed restriction sign show?

options.text: It can be ignored in rain, snow, or ice.
It has a triangle shape.
It is blue with black letters.
It shows a safe speed for a curve or turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It shows a safe speed for a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: Speed signs attached to curve and turn signs show a recommended speed. In fair weather, you might feel safe going faster, but never do so in rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line dividing it. What do you know right away?

options.text: You are on a two-way road.
You are on a one-way road.
The road is being repaired.
You must stay to the left of the yellow lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a two-way road.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means you can pass slower traffic when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: You approach a railroad crossing with no flashing lights or gates. What should you do?

options.text: Cross the tracks immediately and quickly.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Be ready to yield to any train.
Speed up to cross before a train comes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to yield to trains at any railroad crossing. Make sure your entire car can fit on the other side before crossing. Do not shift gears while on the tracks.

questions.question: When parking on a hill, what should you do?

options.text: Touch one rear wheel to the curb.
Use the parking brake and leave the vehicle in park.
Point your front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the parking brake and leave the vehicle in park.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake and put your vehicle in park on a hill. If there is no curb, turn your front wheels so the car will roll away from the road center if brakes fail. If there is a curb, turn your wheels toward it when heading downhill, or away from it when heading uphill.

questions.question: An oncoming car is heading toward you in your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.
Honk, steer left, and brake.
Honk, steer right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, honk, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: Honk to get the other driver's attention. If they don't move, steer right to escape. Don't steer left because the other driver might correct and you will still crash. Brake firmly and steadily to reduce the impact.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, how should you check the traffic?

options.text: Use your rearview and side mirrors.
Use your rearview mirror.
Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see traffic when entering a freeway. This helps you check blind spots and anticipate other vehicles.

questions.question: When must you yield to other drivers?

options.text: When entering the street from a garage or alley.
When a car on your left reaches an unmarked intersection at the same time.
When your traffic light is a green arrow.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering the street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield to other drivers and pedestrians when entering the street from a garage, driveway, or alley.

questions.question: In an area with a 45 mph speed limit or less, how far before turning should you signal?

options.text: 100 feet
200 feet
300 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 100 feet
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before turning when the speed limit is 45 mph or less. For speeds above 45 mph, signal at least 300 feet ahead.

questions.question: Can you pass on a two-lane road when there is a solid yellow line on your side?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass. You may only pass when the broken yellow line is on your side of the road.

questions.question: What can a leaking exhaust system cause?

options.text: Your engine to use too much oil.
Your vehicle to need a tune-up sooner.
You to feel drowsy while driving.
Grass fires on country roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: You to feel drowsy while driving.
questions.explanation: A leaky exhaust system leaks toxic gases that can make you drowsy while driving. These fumes can be dangerous and cause serious harm in a short time.

questions.question: You see a merging traffic sign on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Honk at the incoming traffic.
Keep your speed the same.
Speed up to avoid traffic buildup.
Move to another lane, if it is safe, to let traffic in.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane, if it is safe, to let traffic in.
questions.explanation: When traffic is merging, make room by moving to another lane if it is safe. This helps traffic enter smoothly.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Only use your mirrors.
Start signaling as you move into the next lane.
Signal 500 feet before changing lanes on residential streets.
Always check your blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Other vehicles can be hidden there. Signal 100 feet before turning on residential streets or 5 seconds before changing lanes on a freeway.

questions.question: When entering traffic from an alley or driveway across a sidewalk, what should you do?

options.text: Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.
Stop before driving onto the sidewalk area.
Expect pedestrians to get out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk area.
questions.explanation: Always stop before driving onto a sidewalk or sidewalk area when leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot. Pedestrians and other traffic have the right-of-way.

questions.question: Alcohol is:

options.text: A stimulant.
An antihistamine.
A depressant.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows down your brain and body. It weakens your judgment and makes your reactions slower.

questions.question: Drivers should watch closely for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians because:

options.text: They're difficult to see in traffic.
They obey different traffic laws than larger motor vehicles.
They always have the right-of-way.
They don't have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They're difficult to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians are hard to spot because they are smaller than cars. They may also move quickly or have lights that are easy to miss. Drivers must stay alert to avoid hitting them.

questions.question: You should be careful when passing a bicycle because:

options.text: You are moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass the bicycle.
The cyclist may have to swerve into traffic to avoid an object on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may have to swerve into traffic to avoid an object on the road.
questions.explanation: A cyclist might suddenly move into traffic to avoid something in the road, like a pothole or debris. Always drive carefully around bicycles.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, you should usually:

options.text: Proceed slowly while waiting for an opening.
Accelerate to a speed faster than the freeway traffic.
Turn on your hazard lights until safely on the freeway.
Accelerate to match the speed of freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accelerate to match the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Speed up on the on-ramp to match the freeway traffic. This helps you blend in smoothly and safely. You must yield to cars already on the freeway.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Leave the front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb. This helps stop the car if the brakes fail. On streets without a curb or when parking downhill, turn the wheels toward the curb instead.
